title: Treat a message that starts with a command word as a message
text: In packages/client/src/slash-commands.ts, parseSlash treats any text that starts with a known command name as that command, so a message such as "/new endpoint returns 500" is cleared and run as /new. A command that takes no argument must match only when it is typed alone, so "/new endpoint returns 500" and "/help me fix the build" are messages and parseSlash returns null for them, while "/new" alone is the new command. Commands that do take an argument keep matching with their argument. completeSlash must also put an exact name first, so completing "/pr" offers pr before provider and prompt, with the other matches after it in their usual order.

verification.method: The checks ran in a clean export of the base commit with the hidden files from the solution commit in place, and had to fail. They then ran in a clean export of the solution commit, and had to pass. Installed dependencies were linked from the checkout, and the checks ran with a minimal environment and a temporary home.
